fields.label: Intro sentence
paragraphs: A small moulded rubber stopper that takes the shock out of a closing lid and keeps it from rattling afterwards. It sets how the glove box sounds when it shuts, and it holds that feel for the life of the car — which is a compression-set problem, not a strength one. Compounded for low fogging and low odour, because it lives in the cabin.

Compounded for low fogging and low odour, because it lives in the cabin.

fields.label: Weather is not the question here
paragraphs: On every other part in this catalogue the compound is chosen for what it must survive — oil, ozone, heat, water. On a cabin part the deciding properties are different: low fogging, low odour, and a compression set that holds the interference for a decade at cabin soak temperature.

🛑 And fogging is not a property of the polymer alone. It comes largely from plasticisers, processing aids and residual volatiles — which makes it a compounding and curing decision, exactly the thing Margo does in-house and could sell.
Margo produces every part in every compound it mixes (client-instructed 2026-09-02). Nothing is removed — all eight are ranked on interior criteria rather than weathering.

fields.label: Cards ×4
rows: It has to still be quiet at year five

A stopper that flattens loses its interference and the lid starts to rattle. Compression set is the property this part is really bought on, and we test it in-house to ASTM D395 Method B rather than quoting it from a supplier datasheet.
🛑 It must not fog your windscreen

Interior rubber releases volatiles when a parked car heats up, and they condense as a haze on the glass. Fogging is a compounding decision, not a polymer one — send your limit to DIN 75201 or your own method and we compound to it.

Cabin odour is assessed by a trained panel under heat and humidity, to VDA 270 or your OEM method. Both odour and fogging are normally part of the PPAP submission for an interior part, and we build them into the compound rather than discovering them at approval.
Hardness and interference decide how the lid sounds when it shuts. Too hard and the dashboard sounds hollow; too soft and the lid sits proud. Tell us the feel you want and we will set both.

fields.label: Why industries are the right frame here
paragraphs: A damped closure stop is not tied to one vehicle. The same part quiets any hinged lid that a person opens and shuts — and wherever that lid is in an occupied space, the fogging and odour requirements travel with it. So the industry grid is the correct frame, listing sectors where a cabin or an enclosed interior exists.

sections.title: From compound to certification
sections.chip: Fogging and odour belong in the process
sections.live: LIVE H2 → From Compound to Certification · six steps · the same text as all 31 pages

fields.label: Steps
rows: Material compounding — polymer blending, additive integration and batch QC in our in-house lab. On an interior part the plasticiser and processing-aid package is selected for low fogging and low odour, not only for the physical properties.

Mould design and CNC tool manufacture, in-house, held as a controlled record. Free height and the retaining barb are cut together, since one sets the shut feel and the other keeps the stopper in the panel.
Post-cure and deflashing. Post-curing drives off residual volatiles, which is what keeps an interior part inside its fogging and odour limits.
Quality inspection — dimensional check, hardness, and compression set on batch samples. Fogging and odour are tested against the customer specification at approval.

Export packaging — industrial packing with documentation. Stoppers are bagged loose and uncompressed, since a part stored squashed arrives with the set already in it. ISPM-15 treated pallets where timber packaging is used.
fields.note:
Six steps, six kept. The live text says “ISO-certified lab” in step 01, which becomes “in-house lab”; step 04 is “Post-Cure & Trimming” and gains the volatiles detail.
🛑 Step 04 is where the interior argument becomes a production fact. Post-curing costs oven time and is invisible on delivery, and it is the first thing a cheap supplier drops — then the part fails fogging at approval and nobody knows why.
Step 05 is deliberately careful: it says fogging and odour are tested against the customer specification, not that Margo tests them in-house. That is the honest wording until the testing route is confirmed

notes: The process block must render from the part record.
